editorial.titleTr: Shincheonji's Systematic Party Infiltration Exposed; Ignore It and Face Special Prosecutor
summaryTr: Democratic Party criticized for keeping investigation into Shincheonji group mass membership allegations confidential, evading truth-finding
If organized membership drive and illegal election campaigns confirmed, legal accountability and identification of masterminds essential
Internal factional strife erodes trust in party's own investigation, calls for special prosecutor probe mount
editorial.bodyTr: The Democratic Party has faced criticism for evading truth-finding by failing to disclose its investigation process into allegations of collective entry by Shincheonji members. If systematic recruitment of Shincheonji believers and illegal electioneering are confirmed, legal accountability and investigation into the masterminds behind these activities are necessary. As internal party factional strife has eroded confidence in self-investigation, calls have grown for third-party verification and a formal police inquiry.

editorials.titleTr: Platoon and Company Commanders Fire Warning Shots...Military Discipline in Shambles
summaryTr: A company commander and battalion commander exchanged blank-fire shots at each other during training at an Army unit in the Seoul metropolitan area.
The battalion commander was referred to a military court for failure to control his emotions, claiming the incident was intended as a training instruction.
Military discipline recovery is urgent amid lax security and North Korean threats.
editorials.bodyTr: A captain company commander fired blank rounds during training at an Army unit in the Seoul metropolitan area, and a major battalion commander responded with blanks in turn. The major battalion commander was referred to a military court for failing to control his emotions, explaining that the firing was intended as training guidance. As lapses in vigilance and fence breaches have continued to occur at the military front lines amid growing North Korean threats, military officials have stressed the need to restore military discipline.

summaryTr: Government decides to extend Cheonghae Unit's mission area to southern waters off Oman
Mission expansion makes it possible to balance national protection and U.S. demands
Urgent need to strengthen IoT security in preparation for Iran's refrigerator hacking incident
editorials.bodyTr: The government approved at a state council meeting an extension of the Cheonghae Unit's dispatch that expands its operational area to the southern waters off Oman. An expanded operational area will allow us to protect our merchant ships and citizens more closely while also meeting some of the United States' demands. Since France has identified Iran as the source of cyberattacks on refrigerators, we too must strengthen cybersecurity for internet-connected devices such as home appliances.

summaryTr: Industrial electricity and gas have become more expensive than residential rates due to government price policies.

editorial.titleTr: Editorial: Military Academy Merger Steps Back...Political Logic Must Not Undermine National Security
summaryTr: The Defense Ministry has retreated from its plan to integrate the three military academies, now proposing to keep existing schools intact while consolidating education for only certain periods.
President Lee Jae-myung's remarks about 'erasing the Military Academy' have revealed that the integration is driven by political logic rather than security rationale.
The government should abandon the forced integration effort and focus on strengthening national security through the establishment of a serious educational system.
editorial.bodyTr:
The government's plan to integrate the three military academies, which has been in the works, has now shifted direction toward maintaining existing academies while conducting integrated education at separate facilities for a certain period during the four-year enrollment. Defense Minister Kang Shin-chul revealed this plan during a meeting with the joint alumni association of the three military academies on the 9th, stating, "We have no intention whatsoever of closing down each service academy." Within the military, several proposals are being discussed, including the "1+3 plan" combining one year of integrated education with three years of service-specific advanced training, the "1+2+1 plan" pairing integrated education in the first and fourth years with service-specific education in the second and third years, and establishing a graduate school for integrated education. There are also reports that the government is reviewing a plan to relocate the Army Academy of Korea from Taereung in Seoul to areas near Sejong City while keeping the Naval Academy and Air Force Academy in Jinhae and Cheongju respectively, and to establish a new Armed Forces Academy at Jayoundae for integrated education.

The discussion on military academy integration has been pursued in a backwards manner from the start. Before addressing advanced future warfare, the government should first deliberate what integrated education curriculum cadets need beyond service-specific training and how much time is required for it. Instead, the government has approached the matter by simply merging academies first. The criticism of creating the world's only "naval academy without the sea" and "air force academy without a runway" clearly demonstrates how hastily this integration has been pursued. Moreover, when President Lee Jae-myung stated in August that "all coups have been carried out by Army Academy graduates, but has anyone been held accountable," he ordered swift and strong implementation. This effectively acknowledged that military academy integration is being driven not by the security logic of enhanced jointness that the government has touted, but by political logic aimed at "erasing the Army Academy" in connection with the December 3rd emergency martial law.

The government should now halt the reckless integration push that unsettles military morale and instead establish a serious and meticulous plan to strengthen integrated education for military cadets in fostering a smart, strong military. Should such deliberation conclude that integrated education is necessary, then an appropriate educational system can be developed step by step. Additionally, educational plans for the ROTC and bachelor's officer commissioning programs, which currently comprise the absolute majority of newly commissioned officers, must be reformed in tandem. Education for military cadets who will bear the nation's security is a century-long enterprise. Political considerations must be thoroughly excluded, and the best possible plan should be pursued in service of the greater cause of strengthening national security.

editorial.title: Rising demographic burden
editorial.body: Korea must overhaul education, spending as birth rate falls and population ages A country can postpone a budget debate, but it cannot defer the arrival of a smaller generation. South Korea will see this change in its classrooms: First-grade enrollment for the 2027 academic year is expected to fall below 300,000 for the first time. The 2020 birth cohort numbered 272,337, roughly a quarter of the 1.05 million pupils who entered elementary school at the 1968 peak. The pace of the decline matters. Enrollment fell below 400,000 in 2024 and will drop below 300,000 three years later. Births rose slightly in 2024 and 2025, but those children will not reach school age until 2031 and 2032. Enrollment is projected to fall through 2030. Treating this as a temporary dip, or relying chiefly on subsidies, mistakes a long-term transition for a short-term policy problem. The pressure will move from school gates to public accounts. The country’s old-age dependency ratio, the number of people 65 and older per 100 working-age adults, stands at 31.3 in 2026. It is projected to reach 68.4 by 2045, the highest among OECD members, and 103.3 by 2070. A smaller workforce will have to fund pensions and care for a larger elderly population. Much of that bill is prescribed by law. Spending on elderly programs, including basic pensions and long-term care, is projected to rise 28.7 percent, from 25.7 trillion won ($19.2 billion) in 2026 to 33.1 trillion won in 2030. Statutory welfare spending is forecast to reach 256.7 trillion won that year, up 30.8 percent from 2026. As commitments grow, policymakers will have less room to invest in future growth or respond to downturns. Education finance reveals a similar mismatch. Local education finance grants are pegged partly to 20.79 percent of domestic tax revenue, with education-tax proceeds added, so allocations rise with tax receipts even as pupil numbers fall. From 2016 to 2025, per-student funding nearly doubled, from 7.16 million won to 13.71 million won, even as the school-age population fell from 6.02 million to 5.13 million. A revised formula should redirect some resources beyond primary and secondary schools. Part of the funding could support universities and adult retraining as technology shortens the useful life of skills. School networks need regional planning in cities and remote districts. Blanket closures will leave some children with longer trips to school, but keeping every building open would waste public assets. Teacher- and facility-sharing could preserve access. Cash support alone cannot resolve the conditions shaping family decisions. Housing costs and career penalties weigh heavily on couples. One-off payments cannot readily alter either. Dependable childcare and support for replacement staff when employees at smaller firms take parental leave deserve priority. Even effective family policy will not quickly restore the labor force of a generation ago. A smaller workforce makes participation all the more important. Older adults need more opportunities to remain employed, and women should not face workplace arrangements that penalize long careers. Flexible work and midcareer training can help, but employers must rethink job design. With fewer workers, maintaining output will depend on higher productivity per employee. This demographic adjustment also calls for closer scrutiny of public spending. Central and local governments should eliminate overlapping programs and coordinate health and care services to curb duplicated costs. Low-value programs should face regular review, with funding directed to services that deliver clear social returns. The number of children entering first grade in 2027 was largely set seven years ago. What follows remains a policy choice. 국내 노령부양비, 즉 경제활동 인구 100명당 65세 이상 인구 수는 2026년 현재 31.3명이다. 2045년에는 68.4명에 도달할 것으로 예상되며, 이는 경제협력개발기구(OECD) 회원국 중 가장 높은 수치이고, 2070년에는 103.3명에 이를 것이다. 더 작은 규모의 노동력이 연금을 충당하고 더 많은 고령 인구를 부양해야 한다. 그 비용의 대부분은 법으로 정해져 있다. 기초연금과 장기요양보험을 포함한 고령층 프로그램 지출은 2026년 25조 7000억 원(192억 달러)에서 2030년 33조 1000억 원으로 28.7% 증가할 것으로 예상된다. 법정 복지 지출은 같은 해 256조 7000억 원에 도달할 것으로 전망되며, 이는 2026년 대비 30.8% 증가한 것이다. 의무 지출이 증가하면서 정책 입안자들은 미래 성장에 투자하거나 경기 침체에 대응할 여유가 줄어들 것이다.

교육 재정도 유사한 불균형을 드러낸다. 지역교육재정교부금은 국세 수입의 20.79%에 교육세를 더한 것으로 책정되어 있어, 학령인구가 감소해도 세수에 따라 배분이 증가한다. 2016년부터 2025년까지 학생 1인당 지출은 716만 원에서 1371만 원으로 거의 2배 증가했으며, 같은 기간 학령인구는 602만 명에서 513만 명으로 감소했다. 개정된 공식은 일부 자원을 초중등학교를 넘어 재배분해야 한다. 배분된 재정의 일부는 대학과 성인 재교육을 지원할 수 있으며, 기술 발전은 기술의 유용성 있는 수명을 단축시킨다. 학교 네트워크는 도시와 오지 지역에서 지역 계획이 필요하다. 일괄 폐교는 일부 아이들에게 더 긴 통학거리를 초래하겠지만, 모든 건물을 운영하는 것은 공공 자산을 낭비하는 것이다. 교사와 시설 공유는 접근성을 보존할 수 있다.

현금 지원만으로는 가족의 결정을 좌우하는 조건을 해결할 수 없다. 주택 비용과 경력 페널티는 부부에게 큰 부담을 준다. 일회성 지급금으로는 둘 다 쉽게 바꿀 수 없다. 신뢰할 수 있는 보육 지원과 소규모 기업 직원이 육아휴직을 취할 때 대체 인력에 대한 지원이 우선순위가 되어야 한다. 효과적인 가족정책도 이전 세대 규모의 노동력을 빠르게 회복하지 못할 것이다. 더 작은 규모의 노동력은 참여를 더욱 중요하게 만든다. 고령층은 계속 근로할 기회를 더 많이 필요로 하며, 여성은 경력에 불이익을 주는 직장 환경에 직면해서는 안 된다. 유연한 근무와 경력 중기 교육이 도움이 될 수 있지만, 고용주는 일자리 설계를 재고해야 한다. 노동력이 적어지면서 생산성 유지는 근로자당 더 높은 생산성에 달려 있을 것이다.

이러한 인구 통계학적 조정은 또한 공공 지출에 대한 더 면밀한 검토를 요구한다. 중앙 및 지방 정부는 중복된 프로그램을 제거하고 의료 및 요양 서비스를 조율하여 중복 비용을 억제해야 한다. 낮은 가치의 프로그램은 정기적인 검토에 직면해야 하며, 명확한 사회적 수익을 제공하는 서비스에 자금을 배분해야 한다. 2027년 초등학교 1학년에 입학하는 아이들의 수는 7년 전에 대부분 정해졌다. 이후 과정은 정책 선택의 문제이다. 한국은 더 큰 세대를 법으로 만들어낼 수 없지만, 자신의 제도가 앞으로 가질 인구에 더 나은 서비스를 제공하도록 할 것인지는 결정할 수 있다. 인구 궤적은 대부분 정해졌다. 정부의 대응은 그렇지 않다.

editorials.title: Rising demographic burden
editorials.body: Korea must overhaul education, spending as birth rate falls and population ages A country can postpone a budget debate, but it cannot defer the arrival of a smaller generation. South Korea will see this change in its classrooms: First-grade enrollment for the 2027 academic year is expected to fall below 300,000 for the first time. The 2020 birth cohort numbered 272,337, roughly a quarter of the 1.05 million pupils who entered elementary school at the 1968 peak. The pace of the decline matters. Enrollment fell below 400,000 in 2024 and will drop below 300,000 three years later. Births rose slightly in 2024 and 2025, but those children will not reach school age until 2031 and 2032. Enrollment is projected to fall through 2030. Treating this as a temporary dip, or relying chiefly on subsidies, mistakes a long-term transition for a short-term policy problem. The pressure will move from school gates to public accounts. The country’s old-age dependency ratio, the number of people 65 and older per 100 working-age adults, stands at 31.3 in 2026. It is projected to reach 68.4 by 2045, the highest among OECD members, and 103.3 by 2070. A smaller workforce will have to fund pensions and care for a larger elderly population. Much of that bill is prescribed by law. Spending on elderly programs, including basic pensions and long-term care, is projected to rise 28.7 percent, from 25.7 trillion won ($19.2 billion) in 2026 to 33.1 trillion won in 2030. Statutory welfare spending is forecast to reach 256.7 trillion won that year, up 30.8 percent from 2026. As commitments grow, policymakers will have less room to invest in future growth or respond to downturns. Education finance reveals a similar mismatch. Local education finance grants are pegged partly to 20.79 percent of domestic tax revenue, with education-tax proceeds added, so allocations rise with tax receipts even as pupil numbers fall. From 2016 to 2025, per-student funding nearly doubled, from 7.16 million won to 13.71 million won, even as the school-age population fell from 6.02 million to 5.13 million. A revised formula should redirect some resources beyond primary and secondary schools. Part of the funding could support universities and adult retraining as technology shortens the useful life of skills. School networks need regional planning in cities and remote districts. Blanket closures will leave some children with longer trips to school, but keeping every building open would waste public assets. Teacher- and facility-sharing could preserve access. Cash support alone cannot resolve the conditions shaping family decisions. Housing costs and career penalties weigh heavily on couples. One-off payments cannot readily alter either. Dependable childcare and support for replacement staff when employees at smaller firms take parental leave deserve priority. Even effective family policy will not quickly restore the labor force of a generation ago. A smaller workforce makes participation all the more important. Older adults need more opportunities to remain employed, and women should not face workplace arrangements that penalize long careers. Flexible work and midcareer training can help, but employers must rethink job design. With fewer workers, maintaining output will depend on higher productivity per employee. This demographic adjustment also calls for closer scrutiny of public spending. Central and local governments should eliminate overlapping programs and coordinate health and care services to curb duplicated costs. Low-value programs should face regular review, with funding directed to services that deliver clear social returns. The number of children entering first grade in 2027 was largely set seven years ago. What follows remains a policy choice. Korea cannot legislate a larger generation into existence, but it can decide whether its institutions better serve the population it will have. 이러한 인구 통계학적 조정은 또한 공공 지출에 대한 더 면밀한 검토를 요구한다. 중앙 및 지방 정부는 중복된 프로그램을 제거하고 의료 및 요양 서비스를 조율하여 중복 비용을 억제해야 한다. 낮은 가치의 프로그램은 정기적인 검토에 직면해야 하며, 명확한 사회적 수익을 제공하는 서비스에 자금을 배분해야 한다. 2027년 초등학교 1학년에 입학하는 아이들의 수는 7년 전에 대부분 정해졌다. 이후 과정은 정책 선택의 문제이다. 한국은 더 큰 세대를 법으로 만들어낼 수 없지만, 자신의 제도가 앞으로 가질 인구에 더 나은 서비스를 제공하도록 할 것인지는 결정할 수 있다. 인구 궤적은 대부분 정해졌다. 정부의 대응은 그렇지 않다.

summaryTr: Tripartite dialogue has become the decisive forum for the life and death of the special labor bill.
The government is pushing forward with agenda items including exceptions to the 52-hour workweek and four-year fixed-term employment.
The ruling party's special zone bill's reliance on social dialogue is problematic.
editorial.bodyTr: Tripartite labor-government-business dialogue is becoming the venue that will determine the fate of labor exceptions contained in the Mega-Regional Strategic Industry Special Zone Act. Labor Minister Kim Young-hoon told parliament on the 9th that he will address not only exceptions to the 52-hour workweek but also special provisions allowing fixed-term workers to be employed for up to four years as agenda items in tripartite dialogue. The special zone bill was introduced by the Democratic Party, which holds the majority and is the ruling party. It is the party's responsibility to take ownership and discuss this matter in parliament.
